title: Invited paper: Enhancing Design Automation with Quantum Algorithms for Chip Design
problem: Cell placement optimization to minimize Half-Perimeter Wire Length is computationally expensive in classical approaches, limiting scalability for large designs; quantum and hybrid approaches may offer speedup.
motivation: Chip design resource efficiency (area, power) is strongly correlated with wire length optimization; quantum computing offers potential for accelerating placement optimization, though practical integration with EDA flows remains unproven.
method: The system arranges functional units (called cells) on a chip to minimize the total wire distance needed to connect them—a measure called HPWL, or Half-Perimeter Wire Length. It uses two optimization approaches: a classical method called Simulated Annealing that explores arrangements through random adjustments, and a quantum-based solver from D-Wave that frames the problem as a Constrained Quadratic Model. Both solvers are integrated with OpenROAD, an industry-standard tool for chip physical design and routing. The approach was tested on real chip designs using ASAP7 7nm technology rules.
key_novelty: Combining quantum and hybrid optimization (using D-Wave's Constrained Quadratic Model solver) with OpenROAD, the industry-standard chip design tool, to arrange the functional units on chips.
contributions: Quantum optimization strategy for HPWL minimization using D-Wave CQM solver
Integration with OpenROAD enabling practical validation on real PDK and routing
Comparison of classical (Simulated Annealing) and quantum optimization approaches
Demonstration of better area usage and performance improvements on ASAP7 7nm
Path toward using quantum computers for chip design EDA workloads

metrics.other: Better area usage and considerable speedup/performance improvement

limitations: Preliminary results; scalability to larger designs and quantum advantage over classical not fully demonstrated.
primary_theme: Quantum and hybrid optimization for chip cell placement in EDA
